object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A party that places orders in the system. Each customer is uniquely identified by a customer ID in the CRM.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A sellable item that can be included in orders. Each product is uniquely identified by a stock-keeping unit (SKU) code.

ambiguities.description: Customer vs. Client terminology: The transcript indicates that 'Customer' and 'Client' are used interchangeably by different teams (CRM uses 'Customer', billing uses 'Client'), but the Product Manager notes that the billing team 'has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.' This suggests a potential semantic difference in how the two departments classify the same entities. It is unclear whether 'Client' should be modeled as a subtype of Customer (representing only paying customers), or whether it is truly just an alternative name for the same concept. This may require clarification on whether the model should enforce payment status as a distinguishing factor.

source_references.excerpt: One more thing -- I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Customer name optionality: The transcript states 'every customer has a name,' but does not clarify whether this is enforced at entry time (i.e., is name mandatory during customer creation) or if it can be null/empty in practice. A mandatory constraint has been inferred, but confirmation that name is always populated when a customer is created would strengthen this.

source_references.excerpt: What about the customer's name? Is that tracked? Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

ambiguities.description: Quantity constraint incompleteness: The transcript specifies that an order line includes a product and a quantity, but does not clarify the valid range or constraints on the Quantity value itself. For example, must quantity always be ≥ 1? Can it be 0 or negative? Can it be a decimal (e.g., 2.5 units) or only an integer? The data type is inferred as integer, but the allowed value range is unclear.

ambiguities.description: Customer name uniqueness: It is not stated whether customer names are unique (i.e., can two customers have the same name, or is the combination of name fields unique per customer). The model currently assumes names are not unique, but this should be confirmed.
